messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT — apac1 ingress (envoy) 5xx spike -> 62% errors in the last 2m, p95 latency 1.2s, alerting on-call :rotating_light:
incidents-bot: PagerDuty incident P12345 created and notified oncall (tia-oncall).
pagerduty: Triggered: apac1-ingress-5xx-high (sev2) — routing/ingress errors.

ash-ops: joining the thread, I see the spike on the apac1 envoys. starting live triage.
tia-oncall: oncall here — confirm impact? are customers hitting 502 or 500?
ash-ops: mostly 502/503 from Envoy. Backend target group shows increased TLS handshake failures: "tls: unexpected message" and "connection reset by peer" in envoy logs. short lived but sustained across multiple AZs in apac1.

ev-envoy: past 30s snapshot from envoy access log: 
```
[2026-03-15T12:34:01Z] "POST /api/chat" 502 - 0.003
[2026-03-15T12:34:02Z] "POST /api/embeddings" 503 - 0.001
error: upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers
```

morgan-sre: checking NLB target groups now. seeing healthy host count drop from 18 -> 12 in apac1d. target health shows "unhealthy - TLS handshake" for a subset of hosts.
ben-platform: any recent deploys to the ingress-controller or model-serving pods?
ash-ops: nothing in last 90m, deploy-bot shows last ingress rollout 3h ago.

pagerduty: Note from PD — multiple customers with elevated error rates in APAC, about ~7 customers reporting degraded UX.

ash-ops: hypothesis: ephemeral port exhaustion or conntrack limits on LBs or backend nodes causing half-open connections -> TLS errors. pulling system metrics.
tia-oncall: runbook step 2: check conntrack and ephemeral port usage on nodes and ALB/NLB connection metrics.

ev-envoy: gathered netstat and conntrack snapshot from a failing node: 
```
# sudo conntrack -S | grep entries
entries 182400
# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 196608
```
conntrack usage at ~93%.

morgan-sre: that explains resets. ALB/NLB backed by target nodes are hitting conntrack ceiling -> kernel dropping new connections causing upstream TLS errors.
ben-platform: also seeing a Route53 weighted health-check flip — apac1 weight auto-shifted due to health check failures, some clients still resolving to apac1 due to TTL. cross-region routing churn.

ash-ops: immediate mitigations: 1) scale target group by +30% (add pool in apac1c), 2) bump conntrack on nodes to 400k, 3) reduce Route53 TTL to 20s and set weight 0 for apac1 temporarily to steer traffic to eu-west-1 while we stabilize.

tia-oncall: do that in order. I'll make the Route53 change. morgan, can you do node sysctl change via automation?
morgan-sre: applying sysctl change via Runbook job: 
```
for host in $(cat apac1-node-list); do ssh $host "sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=400000"; done
```
applied to 6/6 nodes, verified conntrack entries dropping to 45% of new limit.

ben-platform: scaling target group: added 6 more targets, health checks passing after retries.

ash-ops: reducing Route53 TTL and setting weight 0 for apac1 now. Command: 
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://apac-weight-zero.json
```
applied, new DNS weight propagation in progress.

customer-success: quick note from CS — customers on APAC region reported intermittent stream disconnects and failing uploads; severity medium but some lost work. notified enterprise contacts.

ev-envoy: restarted ingress controller pods one at a time (kubectl -n ingress rollout restart deployment/ingress-controller). observed drop in 5xx after restarts and conntrack bump.

ash-ops: checking metrics: 5xx rate reduced from 62% -> 8% over 6 minutes. p95 latency back to ~220ms.

pagerduty: Incident P12345 updated to "mitigated" by oncall. Oncall handoff in 30m to morgan-sre for follow-up.

morgan-sre: taking over long-lived investigation and post-incident. Planned follow-ups: increase node conntrack permanently, add ALB/NLB circuit-breaker metrics, add prewarming for TLS handshakes, reduce Route53 TTL to 30s for quicker failovers, instrument target group drain timing.

ben-platform: short-term config change to Envoy -> reduce idle keepalive to 30s and aggressive connection reuse to reduce half-open buildup. Will open PR to infra repo.

ash-ops: customer impact summary for CS: ~7 customers affected, majority transient errors during 12:30-12:40 UTC window, highest impact on streaming/chat features. No data loss reported but degraded UX for session-based flows.

customer-success: copying incident summary to affected customers and offering extended logs and timeline.

tia-oncall: handing off to morgan-sre now. I will remain reachable for 1hr. thanks all. :thumbsup:
morgan-sre: acknowledged, picking up the thread. Starting long-term mitigations and RCA timeline.

incidents-bot: Post-incident checklist recommended: set Sev label: sev2, create incident doc in /incidents/postmortems, assign owners for follow-ups (conntrack->ben-platform, envoy-tuning->ben-platform, dns-ttl->morgan-sre).

morgan-sre: noted. I'll create a postmortem doc and schedule a follow-up within 48h. Closing thread for live mitigation.

ash-ops: thanks everyone. final note: increase monitoring alert thresholds to catch conntrack saturation earlier, add playbook link: #runbooks/conntrack-prevent.

pagerduty: Incident P12345 status: resolved (mitigated) — timeline and follow-ups recorded.

customer-success: confirmed customers notified and support tickets opened for those who asked for extra logs.

morgan-sre: closing handoff. leaving a trace: aws-cloudwatch link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudwatch/home?region=apac-south-1#alarmsV2:alarm/ingress-apac-5xx-spike

incidents-bot: Reminder: please attach logs and runbook steps to the incident document for compliance.
